business_problem: Clarifresh needed to replace a MySQL-on-RDS backend that could not keep up with its expanding multi-cloud footprint, flexible data model needs, and increasingly complex in-app search workloads for produce inspection data.
solution_summary: Clarifresh replatformed its produce-quality application stack from Amazon RDS for MySQL and EC2 to a containerized Java application backed by MongoDB Atlas across both Microsoft Azure and AWS. Field inspectors use iOS and Android apps while managers work in a web application, so the platform had to store varied inspection records, evolve schemas quickly, and stay portable across clouds as the business entered new markets. Atlas became the operational document store for those reports and metadata, removing rigid schema coordination work and letting developers ship features faster. Clarifresh then replaced an indexed $regex search approach with MongoDB Search on Atlas, which can execute parallel index intersections for more complex filtering, and mirrored search behavior locally with the Atlas CLI and Docker so engineers could test new indexes offline before deployment.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Stores Clarifresh's inspection reports and application data in a multi-cloud document database across Azure and AWS.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Search on Atlas
solution_components.role: Indexes report content and filter metadata so inspectors and managers can run low-latency searches inside the application.

data_flow: Produce-quality observations from iOS and Android field apps flow into a containerized Java service backed by MongoDB Atlas on AWS and Azure. Atlas stores inspection reports and metadata, MongoDB Search on Atlas indexes the same documents for the manager web app, and developers test new search indexes locally before promoting them to production.
business_outcome: Clarifresh gained a multi-cloud platform that let developers iterate faster and delivered much faster, more consistent application search for produce inspection workflows.
metrics: Some searches with the original implementation took up to 15 seconds to execute; following the switch to Atlas Search, search time for those searches dropped to 167 milliseconds.
The mean search time took 103 milliseconds prior to adopting Atlas Search and 56 milliseconds after, an improvement of 46%.
architecture_clues: Clarifresh moved from EC2 and Amazon RDS for MySQL to a containerized Java application on MongoDB Atlas across Azure and AWS.
The original search implementation used indexes plus $regex before the team adopted MongoDB Search on Atlas.
Developers use the Atlas CLI and Docker to mirror Atlas Search behavior locally and test new search indexes offline.
